A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed framework is capable of addressing multiple different tasks, and that it can be trained either in a self-supervised or supervised manner.
, for most tracking tasks, a single and task agnostic appearance model can be used to achieve state of the art performance.
, for most tracking tasks, the best approach is to use the same appearance model and to adapt it to the task at hand, instead of using different appearance models for each task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of tracking is more similar than it seems, and the differences in the tasks can be easily addressed within the same framework.
, despite the large diversity in experimental settings, most tracking tasks can indeed be addressed with the same appearance model.
the same appearance-based tracking model can be successfully applied to solve multiple tracking tasks, thus reducing the amount of specialised solutions needed.
